_comment: Dilla — Cloudflare WAF Custom Rules. Import via the Cloudflare API: POST /zones/{zone_id}/rulesets. These rules complement the OWASP CRS rules in deploy/waf/caddy-crs.snippet — Cloudflare WAF runs at the edge; CRS runs on the origin. Tested-with: Cloudflare WAF (Free + Pro), Apr 2026.
name: dilla-waf

rules._comment: 1. Block requests to /api/v1/debug/browser-log from the public internet. The endpoint exists only for local dev; a real client never hits it. R-11 in 03-architecture-review.md also requires JWT, but blocking at the edge is cheaper than authenticating.
rules.description: block public access to debug browser-log

rules._comment: 2. Rate-limit /api/v1/auth/* to 60 req/min/IP. The server already does this via tower_governor; Cloudflare does it before the request crosses the Atlantic.
3. Rate-limit prekey lookups (R-07 / VULN-006 — global-user-deanon path).
4. Block requests with no User-Agent. Real clients always send one; absence is a strong bot signal.
5. Challenge known bad bot UAs. cf.client.bot covers verified bots (Googlebot etc.); we block the rest.
rules.expression: (cf.threat_score gt 30) or (http.user_agent contains "masscan") or (http.user_agent contains "zgrab") or (http.user_agent contains "sqlmap") or (http.user_agent contains "nikto")

rules._comment: 6. Block sensitive paths from non-cf.client.bot anonymous proxies. The federation port is on WG, but defense-in-depth at the edge for the public API.
rules.description: block tor + open proxies on auth surface
rules.expression: (starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/api/v1/auth/")) and (ip.src.country eq "T1" or cf.client.bot eq false and cf.threat_score gt 50)

rules._comment: 7. Block request bodies > 60 MiB. The reverse proxy caps at 50 MiB; this is a belt-and-braces at the edge to prevent slow-loris-with-body attacks.
8. Drop common scanner paths. dilla-server doesn't serve any of these; let the edge eat the traffic.
